## What you should be able to do tonight

- Describe the implied volatility surface as a function of two variables and say what each slice means.
- Compare the implied term structure against your own forecast term structure and interpret the gap.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>65 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Build the surface: implied volatility against log-moneyness and time to expiry, plotted as a surface and as a set of slices. Then convert to total implied variance, which is the coordinate in which the no-arbitrage conditions are cleanest and which tomorrow needs.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Overlay your own forecast: your GARCH or HAR variance term structure from week 13 against the implied one, both annualised. The systematic gap between them is the variance risk premium, which week 40 measures properly. Note its sign and rough magnitude now.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [10 min]{.task-min} Note the practical problem: quotes exist only at listed strikes and expiries, so a surface is an interpolation, and every interpolation choice can create an arbitrage. That is tomorrow.
:::
:::
